4Q7FTjhvZ7Y.title: Project Code Rush - The Beginnings of Netscape / Mozilla Documentary
4Q7FTjhvZ7Y.summary: Code Rush is a one-hour documentary following Netscape engineers in Silicon Valley through the company's last year as an independent firm. It covers the Mozilla open-source announcement, the frantic push to ready the source for release by March 31, 1998, and the toll on engineers' lives before the AOL acquisition.
4Q7FTjhvZ7Y.why: HN commenters recommend it as an intimate, embedded look at late-90s web history and the spirit of building something important under pressure.

quote.text: Code Rush, which is an awesome documentary for anyone interested in the history of the Web

5eW6Eagr9XA.title: The Expert Myth
5eW6Eagr9XA.summary: Veritasium examines which experts have real expertise, drawing on chess research and work by Klein and Kahneman. It explains that expertise comes from pattern recognition built through deliberate practice in valid, feedback-rich environments.
5eW6Eagr9XA.why: Frequently recommended in threads on learning, the 10,000 hours rule and deliberate practice as a clearer account of how expertise develops.

quote.text: Veritasium has a really good video on the subject [0], with a much more compelling explanation for what it takes to develop expertise.

vgT4Y30DkaA.title: Threads (1984) ORIGINAL TRAILER [HD 1080p]
vgT4Y30DkaA.summary: The original trailer for Threads, the 1984 British TV film depicting the aftermath of a nuclear attack on Sheffield. The trailer hints at the film's bleak tone.
vgT4Y30DkaA.why: HN commenters use it to point people to Threads, which they call the most harrowing depiction of nuclear war and say should be mandatory viewing.

quote.text: should be mandatory viewing for all people in positions of power

-Ht4qiDRZE8.title: Massive-scale online collaboration | Luis von Ahn
-Ht4qiDRZE8.summary: Luis von Ahn, creator of CAPTCHA and reCAPTCHA, explains how small contributions from many people online can digitize books. He then introduces Duolingo as a way to translate the web while people learn languages.
-Ht4qiDRZE8.why: HN commenters recommend it as the clearest account of human computation and games with a purpose, straight from the inventor.

quote.text: I highly recommend watching the TED talk by Luis von Ahn, creater of CAPTCHA and reCAPTCHA.

4oAB83Z1ydE.title: Think Different
4oAB83Z1ydE.channel: 英倫米高 Michael in England
4oAB83Z1ydE.summary: Apple's classic 'Think Different' commercial, a one-minute spot celebrating creative misfits and innovators. This upload is from 2006.
4oAB83Z1ydE.why: Shared as an emotionally powerful example of great advertising, especially after Steve Jobs died.

quote.text: I must admit that after watching it just now I teared up a bit.

ngpsJKQR_ZE.title: I'm Allowed to Rob You!
ngpsJKQR_ZE.summary: A short anarchist-leaning video by Larken Rose arguing that the Constitution and similar documents cannot legitimately grant anyone the right to take other people's property. It uses a rhetorical 'paper that lets me rob you' setup to challenge belief in political authority.
ngpsJKQR_ZE.why: Libertarian-minded commenters post it in surveillance, government and constitution threads as a red-pill argument that political authority is illusory.

quote.text: Here's all you need to know about the Constitution

D7Sd8A6_fYU.title: CppCon 2016: Dan Saks “extern c: Talking to C Programmers about C++”
D7Sd8A6_fYU.summary: Dan Saks's CppCon 2016 talk on why C programmers resist C++ and how to talk to them about it. He argues that persuasion rarely works by arguing and examines the culture gap between the two communities.
D7Sd8A6_fYU.why: Recommended in C versus C++ and embedded threads as the expert view on adoption and persuasion.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: The mentioned cppcon presentation by Dan Saks is awesome. Highly recommend watching even if you are not interested in C or C++

DC8tO16xdrY.title: Oswald Acted Alone: JFK Assassination Solved (Part 1 of 2)
DC8tO16xdrY.summary: The first part of a long two-part video series by historian Sean Munger arguing, with citations, that Lee Harvey Oswald assassinated President Kennedy and acted alone. It goes through the provable historical facts and addresses conspiracy theories.
DC8tO16xdrY.why: HN commenters recommend it as the most exhaustive, well-sourced rebuttal of JFK conspiracy theories, often when new assassination claims surface.

quote.text: there's an exhaustive two part series by Sean Munger that sets out the many interlocking lines of evidence that Oswald acted alone.

F8sZRBdmqc0.title: Bryan Cantrill on ARC: A Self-Tuning, Low Overhead Replacement Cache [PWL SF] 10/2017
F8sZRBdmqc0.summary: Bryan Cantrill presents the ARC (Adaptive Replacement Cache) paper by Megiddo and Modha at Papers We Love. He opens with a survey of caching strategies before digging into the self-tuning LRU/MFU design.
F8sZRBdmqc0.why: Recommended in cache-algorithm threads as a fun, informative walk through caching strategies and ARC.

quote.text: Bryan Cantrill does a pretty good survey of caching strategies in the intro

-BeTq99LqUo.title: Dangerous tattoo remover from eBay is a MILLION watt laser
-BeTq99LqUo.summary: Styropyro tests an eBay laser tattoo removal device and finds it is a roughly million-watt pulsed laser, powerful enough to ignite air in the beam. He had bought it hoping to salvage an Nd:YAG laser cavity.
-BeTq99LqUo.why: HN mostly cites it as an example of the absurdly powerful lasers sold cheaply online, and a nod to the channel's DIY laser builds.

quote.text: builds insanely strong lasers with basically salvaged junk electronics.

De0Am_QcZiQ.title: Reboot Develop 2017 - Jonathan Blow, Thekla Inc. / Making Game Programming Less Terrible
De0Am_QcZiQ.summary: Jonathan Blow's Reboot Develop 2017 talk on making game programming less terrible, discussing software bloat, slowness and the design goals behind his own programming language.
De0Am_QcZiQ.why: Cited in discussions of software getting slower and of efforts to reduce friction in programming.

NiTsduRreug.title: Stephen Krashen on Language Acquisition
NiTsduRreug.summary: A 15-minute clip of linguist Stephen Krashen discussing language acquisition, drawn from the 1980s. It presents his input hypothesis and the distinction between acquisition and learning.
NiTsduRreug.why: Cited as the source for comprehensible input, the principle behind immersion-based language learning methods and apps.

quote.text: Their method is based on Stephen Krashen's "language acquisition through comprehensible input"[1] and... it just works.

988jPjs1gao.title: John Chowning - Stria (1977)
988jPjs1gao.summary: John Chowning's 1977 computer music piece Stria, composed with FM synthesis, which he discovered in 1967. It unifies timbre and scale structure around the Golden Mean.
988jPjs1gao.why: HN cites it as an example of early academic FM synthesis composition and the Golden Mean in music.

quote.text: work Stria ( ) unifies timbre and scale structure about the Golden Mean as a musical interval.

Akm7ik-H_7U.title: The high cost of free parking
Akm7ik-H_7U.summary: A Vox explainer on how mandatory parking minimums and free parking impose hidden costs on cities. It draws on Donald Shoup's work and gives the history of parking requirements.
Akm7ik-H_7U.why: HN links it as a concise explanation of why free parking is not really free and how parking rules shape cities.

quote.text: IMHO free parking isn't actually free
